digest.component_or_area: op-cert service key provisioning and signing producer chains
propositions: Per-job boto3/SSM/region lookups and process-global state patching in opcert service create coupling, concurrency hazards, and cleanup risks that must be moved to startup validation and binding

Startup must validate and accept exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY, reject invalid inputs (missing, both-set, unreadable, non-regular, malformed, encrypted, non-Ed25519) before service construction, and materialize a single immutable process-owned signer context

Both completion (sign_completion_verdict→signing.sign_manifest→_sign_manifest_under_lock→mint_opcert_record) and plan-review (generation.sign_manifest→attest.py) producer chains must accept and use context-local OpcertSigner bindings supplied by the service, while developer-local paths retain env/genesis resolution

Op-cert application runtime must eliminate SSM/boto3/region dependencies: fetch-secrets.sh materializes the key to a 0600 `:ro`-mounted file before container start, compose env carries only REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (no SSM parameters), and the runtime image requires no boto3

Process-owned key copy must be placed in a 0700 directory with 0600 file permissions, remain stable for the process lifetime, observe replacement only after restart, and cleanup must never modify the deployment source

Concurrent and timed-out jobs must demonstrate context-local isolation of signer/principal/push policy, one immutable startup signer, no workspace push to remote, and existing signature verification compatibility
